subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Talk about relationships between teenagers and parents
Understand a dialogue between a teacher and a student
Use the past simple and past continuous correctly

tf.s: Nasser was falling asleep in class because he was chatting on the Internet all night.
tf.why: Yes! He stayed up late chatting online.

tf.s: Nasser first said he went to bed at ten o'clock.
tf.why: Right, but that was not the real time.

tf.s: Nasser really went to sleep at ten o'clock.
tf.why: He really went to sleep at about three o'clock.

tf.s: Mr Hamed advises Nasser to get more sleep because he has exams soon.
tf.why: Correct! Sleep is important before exams.

tf.s: We use the past continuous for a short completed action.
tf.why: A short completed action uses the past simple.

tf.s: In 'I was doing my homework when my friend knocked', 'knocked' is the action that interrupted.
tf.why: Yes! The past simple shows the shorter, interrupting action.

tf.s: 'Oman won the Gulf Cup in March 2009' uses the past simple.
tf.why: 'Won' is a completed action in the past.

tf.s: 'She was wearing a lovely pink dress' uses the past simple.
tf.why: 'Was wearing' is the past continuous; it describes an ongoing activity.

tf.s: Listening without interrupting can improve communication between teens and parents.
tf.why: Good! Calm listening helps people understand each other.

boxes.q: Why was Nasser falling asleep in class?
o: he was chatting on the Internet all night

boxes.q: What time did Nasser really go to sleep?
boxes.why: He first said ten, but really slept at about three.

boxes.q: Choose: At 4 o'clock yesterday I ___ coffee.
boxes.why: An action in progress at a time in the past uses the past continuous.

boxes.q: Choose: When the phone ___, I answered it.
boxes.why: Two quick completed actions use the past simple.

boxes.q: Choose: We ___ dinner when there was a power cut.
boxes.why: The longer action in progress uses the past continuous.

boxes.q: Which tense shows a completed action?
boxes.why: For example: 'Oman won the Gulf Cup.'

boxes.q: How did Mr Hamed ask his questions?
Choose: J.K. Rowling taught English before she ___ the Harry Potter books.
Which word often goes with the past continuous?
boxes.why: 'While' introduces a longer action in progress.

boxes.q: Which is a good way to improve communication with parents?
boxes.why: Calm talk helps people understand each other.

hunt.q: Tense for an action in progress

mcq.q: What advice does Mr Hamed give Nasser?
o: to get more sleep because he has exams soon
mcq.why: Mr Hamed cares about Nasser's exams.

mcq.q: What does the past continuous describe?
o: an ongoing action in the past
mcq.why: For example: 'She was wearing a lovely pink dress.'

mcq.q: What was Nasser doing all night?
mcq.why: That is why he was tired in class.

mcq.q: Which word introduces a shorter action that interrupts a longer one?
mcq.why: 'I was doing my homework when my friend knocked.'

mcq.q: Choose: When I first lived abroad, I ___ many problems.
mcq.why: The past simple is used for these completed experiences.

mcq.q: Choose: What ___ at four o'clock yesterday afternoon? – I was drinking coffee.
mcq.why: The answer is past continuous, so the question is too.

o: We were having dinner when the lights went out.
We had dinner when the lights were going out.
We have dinner when the lights went out.
We were have dinner when the lights go out.
mcq.why: Longer action = past continuous; interruption = past simple.

mcq.q: In 'I was doing my homework when my friend knocked on the door', why are two different tenses used?
o: 'was doing' is the longer action; 'knocked' is the short action that interrupted it
Both actions are in the future
mcq.why: The two tenses show which action was in progress.

mcq.q: Why does 'The film was so boring that I almost fell asleep' use 'fell' and not 'was falling'?
mcq.why: 'Was falling' would suggest a continuing action.

mcq.q: How did Mr Hamed show he did not believe Nasser?
o: He asked suspiciously what time Nasser really slept
mcq.why: He asked again to find the real time.
